public_rationale: OpenAI reported improved instruction following over GPT-3 on January 27, 2022 [e1]. Its research paper, available March 4, 2022, found no significant improvement on two bias tests, Winogender and CrowSPairs [e2]. These results support overall gains with uneven improvement in this model family [e1, e2]. Google reported an average gain of 5 BLEU points across more than 100 languages on June 8, 2020 [e3]. These examples support the performance component, but none establishes or refutes the rule that versions without overall improvement are withheld from release [e1, e2, e3]. The full claim remains unresolved [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The evidence covers particular model families from two companies, not the full range of systems claimed.
No item documents release criteria or decisions about unsuccessful candidates.
The evaluated InstructGPT research models were not identical to the deployed API versions.
No significant improvement on a test does not establish exactly unchanged performance.
The Google evidence reports an average BLEU gain, without human comparisons.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models and other machine-learning-based AIs, such as machine translation systems, improve overall over time (since unimproved versions aren't released), but they don't improve across the board.

if they haven't improved, they aren't released

statement.excerpt: Large language models and other machine learning based Ais such as machine translation systems do improve overall over time --- if they haven’t improved, they aren’t released --- but they don’t improve across the board.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that successive systems improve in overall task performance, while improvement does not extend to every task, capability, or example. Unchanged performance can establish nonuniform improvement; actual deterioration is not required.
Overall improvement means better performance across a reasonably broad evaluation of the system’s intended tasks. Marcus supplies no particular benchmark or numerical threshold.
The release qualifier is a substantive assertion that versions without overall improvement are withheld. Evidence of successful releases alone does not establish that selection rule.

The observation concerns historical development through publication on 2023-02-17. Because 'over time' supplies no starting date or reporting cycle, the target period has an unspecified start rather than an invented quarterly window.
The release qualifier is part of the observation, not an antecedent that makes this a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations show overall gains alongside tasks, capabilities, or examples that do not improve. Evidence about release decisions also establishes that overall improvement is a condition for releasing successor versions within the claimed scope.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative comparable evaluations undermine the claimed overall improvement or nonuniformity, or a documented successor release lacks overall improvement on a broad evaluation of its intended tasks. A decline on one task alone does not contradict overall improvement.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Broader comparable evaluations and documented release criteria and decisions for systems developed by February 17, 2023, including rejected candidates, could establish both components. A documented successor release without overall improvement on a broad, comparable evaluation of intended tasks would contradict the release qualifier.
